CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is the Regency of Regent Barito Kuala.
2. Regional Government is the Regent together with regional apparatus as elements of the Regional Government administration of Barito Kuala Regency.
3. Family Planning, Women's Empowerment and Child Protection Agency, abbreviated as BKBP3A is the Regional Work Unit of Barito Kuala Regency.
4. Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Children, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is an integrated service unit established by the Regional Government to provide services to women and children victims of violence comprehensively through information services, assistance and legal aid, counseling services, medical services and safe houses through referrals.
5. Task Force for the Prevention and Handling of Human Trafficking Crimes, hereinafter referred to as the Task Force is a coordinating institution tasked with coordinating prevention and handling efforts of human trafficking crimes in Barito Kuala Regency.
6. Woman is a person who has female genitalia who can menstruate and become pregnant or has obtained legal status as a woman.
7. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including those in the womb.
8. Discrimination is any distinction, harassment or exclusion that is direct or indirect based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, class, social status, socio-economic status, gender, language, political beliefs that result in reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural and other aspects of life.
9. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, psychological to the victim;
10. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions. Coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life;
11. Violence against children is any act that results in misery or suffering to children physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom.
12. Domestic violence is any act against a person, especially women, that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically and or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion or deprivation of freedom unlawfully within the scope of the household;
13. Human trafficking is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud, and abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited;
14. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and or causing death.
15. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and or certain purposes.
16. Economic violence is any act that deliberately neglects family members in the form of not providing a decent living, care or maintenance.
17. Psychological violence is any act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and or severe psychological suffering to a person.
18. Victim is a woman and child who experiences and/or suffers either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
19. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the Police, Prosecutor's Office, Court, Social Institutions, or other parties who know or hear or violence against women has occurred.
20. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
21. Companion is a person who has the expertise to accompany victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
22. Optimal service is a dynamic effort consisting of various parts that are regularly related, followed by performance offered by one party to another party by providing benefits, in order to achieve the best goal.
23. Information is a message (speech or expression) or collection of messages consisting of order sequences of symbols, or meanings that can be interpreted from messages or collections of messages and can be recorded or transmitted.
24. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and or mother;
25. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and his children, and mother and her children and among people who are their dependents.
26. Society is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.

Article 3

Point a
What is meant by trafficking in persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, falsification of documents or identity, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control or other person, whether carried out within the country or between countries for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited.

Point b
What is meant by exploitation is an act with or without the consent of the victim which includes prostitution, forced labor or service, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, utilization of sexual physical reproductive organs or unlawfully, transferring/utilizing labor or transplanting organs and or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial.

Point c
Sufficiently clear.

Point d
What is meant by witness is a person who sees, hears and experiences events of violence and human rights violations.

Point e
Mediation is carried out for cases of domestic violence that fall into the category of complaint offenses as regulated in Law No. 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence.

Article 8

1. The obligations and responsibilities of the community as referred to in Article 6 letter b, shall be implemented in the form of community participation.
2. Forms of community participation as referred to in paragraph (1), include:
a. preventing the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children;
b. providing information and/or reporting acts of violence against women and children to law enforcement or authorized parties; and
c. participating in providing assistance and/or handling victims of acts of violence.
3. Forms of community participation as referred to in paragraph (2), shall be carried out responsibly in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

NUMBER 4 OF 2015

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN FROM ACTS OF VIOLENCE

BY THE GRACE OF ALMIGHTY GOD

THE REGENT OF BARITO KUALA,

Considering:

a. that discrimination and violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights and crimes against humanity; b. that in the context of fulfilling the constitutional rights of women and children as well as to improve the quality of life of women and children is one of the mandatory affairs that is the duty, authority and responsibility of the regional government; c. that discrimination and violence against women and children in Barito Kuala Regency continues to increase and spread, causing community members to be unsafe in carrying out their lives, thus requiring integrated protection efforts; d. that based on the considerations as referred to in letter a, letter b, and letter c, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children from Acts of Violence; In View of:

CHAPTER VII

INSTITUTIONAL ARRANGEMENTS

Article 16

1. In the context of providing protection services to women and children from acts of violence, the regional government establishes P2TP2A as an integrated service center for the protection of women and children from acts of violence including victims of acts of violence.
2. P2TP2A as referred to in paragraph (1), functions as an integrated service center in providing protection to women and children from acts of violence.
3. Further provisions regarding the Organization and Work Procedures of P2TP2A as referred to in paragraph (1), shall be stipulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 21

1. The regional government establishes partnerships with the business sector in the protection of women and children from acts of violence.
2. Partnership as referred to in paragraph (1) is conducted through:
a. notification of employment opportunity information for women victims of acts of violence;
b. education and training for women victims of acts of violence;
c. educational assistance for women and children victims of acts of violence who have been withdrawn from their education; and
d. fostering and increasing the economic independence of women victims of acts of violence.
3. Partnership as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2), shall be set forth in the form of an agreement.

Article 23

1. The regional government is obliged to conduct supervision of the implementation of protection of women and children from acts of violence.
2. Supervision as referred to in paragraph (1), is conducted with professional, transparent, and accountable principles.

CHAPTER IX

GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION

Article 22

1. The Regional Government is obliged to conduct guidance and supervision of the implementation of protection of women and children from acts of violence.
2. Guidance as referred to in paragraph (1), includes:
a. guidelines and fulfillment standards;
b. technical guidance and training;
c. provision of facilities;
d. monitoring; and
e. evaluation.
3. Guidance as referred to in paragraph (2), is in order to realize the objectives of protection of women and children from acts of violence in accordance with minimum service standards implemented by SKPD and the community.

To Establish:
REGIONAL REGULATION CONCERNING THE PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN FROM ACTS OF VIOLENCE.

Article 9

The obligations of family and/or parents as referred to in Article 6 letters c and d, who legally have full responsibility to prevent all forms of violence and protect women and children as family members.

Article 12

Paragraph (1)
Point a
What is meant by complaint service is a series of actions carried out by the organizer of the integrated service institution to follow up on reports of acts of violence against women and children submitted by victims, families and/or the community.

Point b
What is meant by health services is an effort that includes promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative aspects.

Point c
What is meant by legal assistance is legal services provided by legal assistants or advocates to carry out the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of violence against women and children that is gender sensitive.

Point d
What is meant by repatriation is returning women and child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point or from the receiving area to the area of origin.

Point e
What is meant by social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly.

What is meant by social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.

Point f
What is meant by assistance service is that victims have the right to be accompanied by social workers at the investigation, prosecution or examination level.

Paragraph (2)
What is meant by minimum service standards is a performance benchmark for integrated service units in providing complaint handling services, health services, social rehabilitation, law enforcement and legal assistance, as well as repatriation and social reintegration for women and child victims of violence.

Paragraph (3)
Sufficiently clear.

Article 13

The regional government is obligated to provide complaint services for the protection of women and children from acts of violence.

Article 22

Paragraph (1)
what is meant by guidance on the implementation of prevention and protection of women and children from acts of violence is an effort undertaken by the regional government and the community to realize the achievement of the objectives of prevention and protection of women and children from acts of violence.

What is meant by supervision of the implementation of prevention and protection of women and children from acts of violence is a process of activities aimed at ensuring that efforts undertaken by the regional government and the community run efficiently and effectively in accordance with plans and provisions of laws and regulations.

Paragraph (2)
Sufficiently clear.

Paragraph (3)
Sufficiently clear.

Article 26

1. The regional government may provide financial assistance to community organizations, social organizations or non-governmental organizations that implement protection of women and children from discrimination and acts of violence.
2. Financial assistance as referred to in paragraph (1), is in accordance with regional financial capacity, and is implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations in the field of regional finance.

I. GENERAL

The State has an obligation to provide a sense of security to its citizens from threats and actions that can disturb and damage psychological (psychic), physical, sexual and economic security. This is philosophically stated in the preamble of the 1945 Constitution, that the purpose of the establishment of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia is to protect the entire Nation and Homeland of Indonesia.

Therefore, the Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women), and is therefore obliged to fulfill these provisions.

Human Rights state that, the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the State, especially the Government. Through Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection, the Government recognizes the existence of children's rights. The inherent rights of children include basic rights as human beings, namely the Right to Life, the Right to Growth and Development, the Right to Protection and the Right to Participation.

Protection is needed to prevent physical, mental and sexual violence and exploitation. To fulfill the right to growth and development, children need space to play, exercise, and education that is appropriate to their physical and psychological development. In fulfilling children's rights, every government administrator, community and parents are obliged to understand and care about children's rights. The existence of legal instruments and law enforcement officials who defend the interests of children is needed for this protection effort. Laws and regulations that are principled to defend the best interests of the child are needed to realize protection that is legal in nature.

The Government of Barito Kuala Regency has established the Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment (P2TP2A) as a center for empowerment of women victims of acts of violence which specifically has the main duties and functions for empowerment of women and children victims of acts of violence.

From the above framework, the Government of Barito Kuala Regency is responsible for taking legal actions to prevent, suppress, reduce, and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children, by making a Regional Regulation of Barito Kuala Regency concerning Protection of Women and Children from Acts of Violence.

Article 4

Point a
What is meant by the right to have one's dignity respected is upholding human rights.

Point b
Sufficiently clear.

Point c
Sufficiently clear.

Point d
What is meant by the right to information is the right to obtain information, statements, ideas, and signs that contain value, meaning and messages, whether data, facts or explanations that can be seen, heard, and read presented in various packages and formats in accordance with the development of information and communication technology both electronically and non-electronically related to acts of violence.

Point e
Sufficiently clear.

Point f
What is meant by the right to compensation includes economic empowerment, repatriation costs, health insurance, and education or skills.

Point g
What is meant by the victim's right to rehabilitation includes: access to medical services for physical and psychological recovery, legal assistance to restore civil rights, restoration of good name, citizenship.

Point h
What is meant by the right to complaint handling is the availability of a special integrated service unit by officers.

Point i
Sufficiently clear.

Point j
What is meant by the right to assistance includes among others psychologists, psychiatrists, health experts, clergy, advocates and family members.

What is meant by assistant is an individual who works as a volunteer to provide protection and support to women and children who are victims of acts of violence during the judicial process, these assistants can come from family members, friends or independent organizations that provide attention to witnesses and victims or advocates.

Sufficiently clear.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is the Regency of Regent Barito Kuala.
2. Regional Government is the Regent together with regional apparatus as elements of the Regional Government administration of Barito Kuala Regency.
3. Family Planning, Women's Empowerment and Child Protection Agency, abbreviated as BKBP3A is the Regional Work Unit of Barito Kuala Regency.
4. Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Children, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is an integrated service unit established by the Regional Government to provide services to women and children victims of violence comprehensively through information services, assistance and legal aid, counseling services, medical services and safe houses through referrals.
5. Task Force for the Prevention and Handling of Human Trafficking Crimes, hereinafter referred to as the Task Force is a coordinating institution tasked with coordinating prevention and handling efforts of human trafficking crimes in Barito Kuala Regency.
6. Woman is a person who has female genitalia who can menstruate and become pregnant or has obtained legal status as a woman.
7. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including those in the womb.
8. Discrimination is any distinction, harassment or exclusion that is direct or indirect based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, class, social status, socio-economic status, gender, language, political beliefs that result in reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural and other aspects of life.
9. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, psychological to the victim;
10. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions. Coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life;
11. Violence against children is any act that results in misery or suffering to children physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom.
12. Domestic violence is any act against a person, especially women, that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically and or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion or deprivation of freedom unlawfully within the scope of the household;
13. Human trafficking is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud, and abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited;
14. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and or causing death.
15. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and or certain purposes.
16. Economic violence is any act that deliberately neglects family members in the form of not providing a decent living, care or maintenance.
17. Psychological violence is any act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and or severe psychological suffering to a person.
18. Victim is a woman and child who experiences and/or suffers either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
19. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the Police, Prosecutor's Office, Court, Social Institutions, or other parties who know or hear or violence against women has occurred.
20. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
21. Companion is a person who has the expertise to accompany victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
22. Optimal service is a dynamic effort consisting of various parts that are regularly related, followed by performance offered by one party to another party by providing benefits, in order to achieve the best goal.
23. Information is a message (speech or expression) or collection of messages consisting of order sequences of symbols, or meanings that can be interpreted from messages or collections of messages and can be recorded or transmitted.
24. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and or mother;
25. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and his children, and mother and her children and among people who are their dependents.
26. Society is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.

I. GENERAL

The State has an obligation to provide a sense of security to its citizens from threats and actions that can disturb and damage psychological (psychic), physical, sexual and economic security. This is philosophically stated in the preamble of the 1945 Constitution, that the purpose of the establishment of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia is to protect the entire Nation and Homeland of Indonesia.

Therefore, the Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women), and is therefore obliged to fulfill these provisions.

Human Rights state that, the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the State, especially the Government. Through Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection, the Government recognizes the existence of children's rights. The inherent rights of children include basic rights as human beings, namely the Right to Life, the Right to Growth and Development, the Right to Protection and the Right to Participation.

Protection is needed to prevent physical, mental and sexual violence and exploitation. To fulfill the right to growth and development, children need space to play, exercise, and education that is appropriate to their physical and psychological development. In fulfilling children's rights, every government administrator, community and parents are obliged to understand and care about children's rights. The existence of legal instruments and law enforcement officials who defend the interests of children is needed for this protection effort. Laws and regulations that are principled to defend the best interests of the child are needed to realize protection that is legal in nature.

The Government of Barito Kuala Regency has established the Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment (P2TP2A) as a center for empowerment of women victims of acts of violence which specifically has the main duties and functions for empowerment of women and children victims of acts of violence.

From the above framework, the Government of Barito Kuala Regency is responsible for taking legal actions to prevent, suppress, reduce, and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children, by making a Regional Regulation of Barito Kuala Regency concerning Protection of Women and Children from Acts of Violence.

Discrimination is any distinction, harassment or exclusion that is direct or indirect based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, class, social status, socio-economic status, gender, language, political beliefs that result in reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural and other aspects of life.
9. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, psychological to the victim;
10. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions. Coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life;
11. Violence against children is any act that results in misery or suffering to children physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom.
12. Domestic violence is any act against a person, especially women, that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically and or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion or deprivation of freedom unlawfully within the scope of the household;
13. Human trafficking is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud, and abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited;
14. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and or causing death.
15. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and or certain purposes.
16. Economic violence is any act that deliberately neglects family members in the form of not providing a decent living, care or maintenance.
17. Psychological violence is any act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and or severe psychological suffering to a person.
18. Victim is a woman and child who experiences and/or suffers either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
19. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the Police, Prosecutor's Office, Court, Social Institutions, or other parties who know or hear or violence against women has occurred.
20. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
21. Companion is a person who has the expertise to accompany victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
22. Optimal service is a dynamic effort consisting of various parts that are regularly related, followed by performance offered by one party to another party by providing benefits, in order to achieve the best goal.

I. GENERAL

The State has an obligation to provide a sense of security to its citizens from threats and actions that can disturb and damage psychological (psychic), physical, sexual and economic security. This is philosophically stated in the preamble of the 1945 Constitution, that the purpose of the establishment of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia is to protect the entire Nation and Homeland of Indonesia.

Therefore, the Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women), and is therefore obliged to fulfill these provisions.

Human Rights state that, the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the State, especially the Government. Through Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection, the Government recognizes the existence of children's rights. The inherent rights of children include basic rights as human beings, namely the Right to Life, the Right to Growth and Development, the Right to Protection and the Right to Participation.

Protection is needed to prevent physical, mental and sexual violence and exploitation. To fulfill the right to growth and development, children need space to play, exercise, and education that is appropriate to their physical and psychological development. In fulfilling children's rights, every government administrator, community and parents are obliged to understand and care about children's rights. The existence of legal instruments and law enforcement officials who defend the interests of children is needed for this protection effort. Laws and regulations that are principled to defend the best interests of the child are needed to realize protection that is legal in nature.

The Government of Barito Kuala Regency has established the Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment (P2TP2A) as a center for empowerment of women victims of acts of violence which specifically has the main duties and functions for empowerment of women and children victims of acts of violence.

From the above framework, the Government of Barito Kuala Regency is responsible for taking legal actions to prevent, suppress, reduce, and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children, by making a Regional Regulation of Barito Kuala Regency concerning Protection of Women and Children from Acts of Violence.

8. Discrimination is any distinction, harassment or exclusion that is direct or indirect based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, class, social status, socio-economic status, gender, language, political beliefs that result in reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural and other aspects of life.
9. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, psychological to the victim;

Coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life;

I. GENERAL

The State has an obligation to provide a sense of security to its citizens from threats and actions that can disturb and damage psychological (psychic), physical, sexual and economic security. This is philosophically stated in the preamble of the 1945 Constitution, that the purpose of the establishment of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia is to protect the entire Nation and Homeland of Indonesia.

Therefore, the Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women), and is therefore obliged to fulfill these provisions.

Human Rights state that, the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the State, especially the Government. Through Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection, the Government recognizes the existence of children's rights. The inherent rights of children include basic rights as human beings, namely the Right to Life, the Right to Growth and Development, the Right to Protection and the Right to Participation.

Protection is needed to prevent physical, mental and sexual violence and exploitation. To fulfill the right to growth and development, children need space to play, exercise, and education that is appropriate to their physical and psychological development. In fulfilling children's rights, every government administrator, community and parents are obliged to understand and care about children's rights. The existence of legal instruments and law enforcement officials who defend the interests of children is needed for this protection effort. Laws and regulations that are principled to defend the best interests of the child are needed to realize protection that is legal in nature.

The Government of Barito Kuala Regency has established the Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment (P2TP2A) as a center for empowerment of women victims of acts of violence which specifically has the main duties and functions for empowerment of women and children victims of acts of violence.

From the above framework, the Government of Barito Kuala Regency is responsible for taking legal actions to prevent, suppress, reduce, and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children, by making a Regional Regulation of Barito Kuala Regency concerning Protection of Women and Children from Acts of Violence.

2. Financial assistance as referred to in paragraph (1), is in accordance with regional financial capacity, and is implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations in the field of regional finance.

Article 2

Point a

Point b
The principle of justice and gender equality means that gender justice is a process to be fair to men and women. Gender equality is the equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings so that they are able to play a role and participate in political, economic, social, cultural, governmental activities and equality in enjoying the results of development.

Point c
The principle of protection is a principle that functions to provide protection to women and children in order to provide peace in family and community life.

Point d
The principle of the best interests of women and children, that all actions concerning women and children carried out by families, communities, and Regional Government to fulfill the rights of women and children as regulated in laws and regulations.
Point e
The principle of non-discrimination, that in providing protection to women and children from acts of violence there is no discrimination based on age, sex, race, ethnicity, tribe, religion and between groups.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

2. Regional Government is the Regent together with regional apparatus as elements of the Regional Government administration of Barito Kuala Regency.
3. Family Planning, Women's Empowerment and Child Protection Agency, abbreviated as BKBP3A is the Regional Work Unit of Barito Kuala Regency.
4. Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Children, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is an integrated service unit established by the Regional Government to provide services to women and children victims of violence comprehensively through information services, assistance and legal aid, counseling services, medical services and safe houses through referrals.
5. Task Force for the Prevention and Handling of Human Trafficking Crimes, hereinafter referred to as the Task Force is a coordinating institution tasked with coordinating prevention and handling efforts of human trafficking crimes in Barito Kuala Regency.
6. Woman is a person who has female genitalia who can menstruate and become pregnant or has obtained legal status as a woman.
7. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including those in the womb.
8. Discrimination is any distinction, harassment or exclusion that is direct or indirect based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, class, social status, socio-economic status, gender, language, political beliefs that result in reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural and other aspects of life.
9. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, psychological to the victim;
10. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions. Coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life;
11. Violence against children is any act that results in misery or suffering to children physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom.
12. Domestic violence is any act against a person, especially women, that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically and or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion or deprivation of freedom unlawfully within the scope of the household;
13. Human trafficking is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud, and abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited;
14. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and or causing death.
15. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and or certain purposes.
16. Economic violence is any act that deliberately neglects family members in the form of not providing a decent living, care or maintenance.
17. Psychological violence is any act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and or severe psychological suffering to a person.
18. Victim is a woman and child who experiences and/or suffers either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
19. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the Police, Prosecutor's Office, Court, Social Institutions, or other parties who know or hear or violence against women has occurred.
20. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
21. Companion is a person who has the expertise to accompany victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
22. Optimal service is a dynamic effort consisting of various parts that are regularly related, followed by performance offered by one party to another party by providing benefits, in order to achieve the best goal.
23. Information is a message (speech or expression) or collection of messages consisting of order sequences of symbols, or meanings that can be interpreted from messages or collections of messages and can be recorded or transmitted.
24. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and or mother;
25. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and his children, and mother and her children and among people who are their dependents.
26. Society is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.

3. Family Planning, Women's Empowerment and Child Protection Agency, abbreviated as BKBP3A is the Regional Work Unit of Barito Kuala Regency.
4. Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Children, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is an integrated service unit established by the Regional Government to provide services to women and children victims of violence comprehensively through information services, assistance and legal aid, counseling services, medical services and safe houses through referrals.
5. Task Force for the Prevention and Handling of Human Trafficking Crimes, hereinafter referred to as the Task Force is a coordinating institution tasked with coordinating prevention and handling efforts of human trafficking crimes in Barito Kuala Regency.
6. Woman is a person who has female genitalia who can menstruate and become pregnant or has obtained legal status as a woman.
7. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including those in the womb.
8. Discrimination is any distinction, harassment or exclusion that is direct or indirect based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, class, social status, socio-economic status, gender, language, political beliefs that result in reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural and other aspects of life.
9. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, psychological to the victim;
10. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions. Coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life;
11. Violence against children is any act that results in misery or suffering to children physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom.
12. Domestic violence is any act against a person, especially women, that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically and or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion or deprivation of freedom unlawfully within the scope of the household;
13. Human trafficking is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud, and abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited;
14. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and or causing death.
15. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and or certain purposes.
16. Economic violence is any act that deliberately neglects family members in the form of not providing a decent living, care or maintenance.
17. Psychological violence is any act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and or severe psychological suffering to a person.
18. Victim is a woman and child who experiences and/or suffers either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
19. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the Police, Prosecutor's Office, Court, Social Institutions, or other parties who know or hear or violence against women has occurred.
20. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
21. Companion is a person who has the expertise to accompany victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
22. Optimal service is a dynamic effort consisting of various parts that are regularly related, followed by performance offered by one party to another party by providing benefits, in order to achieve the best goal.
23. Information is a message (speech or expression) or collection of messages consisting of order sequences of symbols, or meanings that can be interpreted from messages or collections of messages and can be recorded or transmitted.
24. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and or mother;
25. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and his children, and mother and her children and among people who are their dependents.
26. Society is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.

I. GENERAL

The State has an obligation to provide a sense of security to its citizens from threats and actions that can disturb and damage psychological (psychic), physical, sexual and economic security. This is philosophically stated in the preamble of the 1945 Constitution, that the purpose of the establishment of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia is to protect the entire Nation and Homeland of Indonesia.

Therefore, the Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women), and is therefore obliged to fulfill these provisions.

Human Rights state that, the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the State, especially the Government. Through Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection, the Government recognizes the existence of children's rights. The inherent rights of children include basic rights as human beings, namely the Right to Life, the Right to Growth and Development, the Right to Protection and the Right to Participation.

Protection is needed to prevent physical, mental and sexual violence and exploitation. To fulfill the right to growth and development, children need space to play, exercise, and education that is appropriate to their physical and psychological development. In fulfilling children's rights, every government administrator, community and parents are obliged to understand and care about children's rights. The existence of legal instruments and law enforcement officials who defend the interests of children is needed for this protection effort. Laws and regulations that are principled to defend the best interests of the child are needed to realize protection that is legal in nature.

The Government of Barito Kuala Regency has established the Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment (P2TP2A) as a center for empowerment of women victims of acts of violence which specifically has the main duties and functions for empowerment of women and children victims of acts of violence.

From the above framework, the Government of Barito Kuala Regency is responsible for taking legal actions to prevent, suppress, reduce, and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children, by making a Regional Regulation of Barito Kuala Regency concerning Protection of Women and Children from Acts of Violence.

Article 18

1. The task force as referred to in Article 17 letter a, shall consist of representatives from the regional government, law enforcement, community organizations, non-governmental organizations, professional organizations, and researchers/academics.
2. The task force as referred to in paragraph (1), is a coordinative institution tasked with coordinating the prevention and handling of trafficking in persons.
3. Further provisions regarding the establishment, duties, and functions of the task force as referred to in paragraph (1), shall be stipulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 23

1. The regional government is obliged to conduct supervision of the implementation of protection of women and children from acts of violence.
2. Supervision as referred to in paragraph (1), is conducted with professional, transparent, and accountable principles.

CHAPTER IX

GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION

Article 22

1. The Regional Government is obliged to conduct guidance and supervision of the implementation of protection of women and children from acts of violence.
2. Guidance as referred to in paragraph (1), includes:
a. guidelines and fulfillment standards;
b. technical guidance and training;
c. provision of facilities;
d. monitoring; and
e. evaluation.
3. Guidance as referred to in paragraph (2), is in order to realize the objectives of protection of women and children from acts of violence in accordance with minimum service standards implemented by SKPD and the community.

Article 8

1. The obligations and responsibilities of the community as referred to in Article 6 letter b, shall be implemented in the form of community participation.
2. Forms of community participation as referred to in paragraph (1), include:
a. preventing the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children;
b. providing information and/or reporting acts of violence against women and children to law enforcement or authorized parties; and
c. participating in providing assistance and/or handling victims of acts of violence.
3. Forms of community participation as referred to in paragraph (2), shall be carried out responsibly in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 21

1. The regional government establishes partnerships with the business sector in the protection of women and children from acts of violence.
2. Partnership as referred to in paragraph (1) is conducted through:
a. notification of employment opportunity information for women victims of acts of violence;
b. education and training for women victims of acts of violence;
c. educational assistance for women and children victims of acts of violence who have been withdrawn from their education; and
d. fostering and increasing the economic independence of women victims of acts of violence.
3. Partnership as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2), shall be set forth in the form of an agreement.

BY THE GRACE OF ALMIGHTY GOD

THE REGENT OF BARITO KUALA,

Article 2

Point a
The principle of humanity becomes the foundation of the concept of protection of women and children from acts of violence, which is respect for human rights and the dignity of every citizen and resident of Indonesia proportionally (the second principle of Pancasila).

Point b
The principle of justice and gender equality means that gender justice is a process to be fair to men and women. Gender equality is the equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings so that they are able to play a role and participate in political, economic, social, cultural, governmental activities and equality in enjoying the results of development.

Point c
The principle of protection is a principle that functions to provide protection to women and children in order to provide peace in family and community life.

Point d
The principle of the best interests of women and children, that all actions concerning women and children carried out by families, communities, and Regional Government to fulfill the rights of women and children as regulated in laws and regulations.
Point e
The principle of non-discrimination, that in providing protection to women and children from acts of violence there is no discrimination based on age, sex, race, ethnicity, tribe, religion and between groups.

I. GENERAL

The State has an obligation to provide a sense of security to its citizens from threats and actions that can disturb and damage psychological (psychic), physical, sexual and economic security. This is philosophically stated in the preamble of the 1945 Constitution, that the purpose of the establishment of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia is to protect the entire Nation and Homeland of Indonesia.

Therefore, the Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women), and is therefore obliged to fulfill these provisions.

Human Rights state that, the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the State, especially the Government. Through Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection, the Government recognizes the existence of children's rights. The inherent rights of children include basic rights as human beings, namely the Right to Life, the Right to Growth and Development, the Right to Protection and the Right to Participation.

Protection is needed to prevent physical, mental and sexual violence and exploitation. To fulfill the right to growth and development, children need space to play, exercise, and education that is appropriate to their physical and psychological development. In fulfilling children's rights, every government administrator, community and parents are obliged to understand and care about children's rights. The existence of legal instruments and law enforcement officials who defend the interests of children is needed for this protection effort. Laws and regulations that are principled to defend the best interests of the child are needed to realize protection that is legal in nature.

The Government of Barito Kuala Regency has established the Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment (P2TP2A) as a center for empowerment of women victims of acts of violence which specifically has the main duties and functions for empowerment of women and children victims of acts of violence.

From the above framework, the Government of Barito Kuala Regency is responsible for taking legal actions to prevent, suppress, reduce, and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children, by making a Regional Regulation of Barito Kuala Regency concerning Protection of Women and Children from Acts of Violence.

Therefore, the Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women), and is therefore obliged to fulfill these provisions.

Human Rights state that, the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the State, especially the Government. Through Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection, the Government recognizes the existence of children's rights. The inherent rights of children include basic rights as human beings, namely the Right to Life, the Right to Growth and Development, the Right to Protection and the Right to Participation.

Protection is needed to prevent physical, mental and sexual violence and exploitation. To fulfill the right to growth and development, children need space to play, exercise, and education that is appropriate to their physical and psychological development. In fulfilling children's rights, every government administrator, community and parents are obliged to understand and care about children's rights. The existence of legal instruments and law enforcement officials who defend the interests of children is needed for this protection effort. Laws and regulations that are principled to defend the best interests of the child are needed to realize protection that is legal in nature.

The Government of Barito Kuala Regency has established the Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment (P2TP2A) as a center for empowerment of women victims of acts of violence which specifically has the main duties and functions for empowerment of women and children victims of acts of violence.

From the above framework, the Government of Barito Kuala Regency is responsible for taking legal actions to prevent, suppress, reduce, and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children, by making a Regional Regulation of Barito Kuala Regency concerning Protection of Women and Children from Acts of Violence.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is the Regency of Regent Barito Kuala.
2. Regional Government is the Regent together with regional apparatus as elements of the Regional Government administration of Barito Kuala Regency.
3. Family Planning, Women's Empowerment and Child Protection Agency, abbreviated as BKBP3A is the Regional Work Unit of Barito Kuala Regency.
4. Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Children, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is an integrated service unit established by the Regional Government to provide services to women and children victims of violence comprehensively through information services, assistance and legal aid, counseling services, medical services and safe houses through referrals.
5. Task Force for the Prevention and Handling of Human Trafficking Crimes, hereinafter referred to as the Task Force is a coordinating institution tasked with coordinating prevention and handling efforts of human trafficking crimes in Barito Kuala Regency.
6. Woman is a person who has female genitalia who can menstruate and become pregnant or has obtained legal status as a woman.
7. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including those in the womb.
8. Discrimination is any distinction, harassment or exclusion that is direct or indirect based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, class, social status, socio-economic status, gender, language, political beliefs that result in reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural and other aspects of life.
9. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, psychological to the victim;
10. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions. Coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life;
11. Violence against children is any act that results in misery or suffering to children physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom.
12. Domestic violence is any act against a person, especially women, that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically and or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion or deprivation of freedom unlawfully within the scope of the household;
13. Human trafficking is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud, and abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited;
14. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and or causing death.
15. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and or certain purposes.
16. Economic violence is any act that deliberately neglects family members in the form of not providing a decent living, care or maintenance.
17. Psychological violence is any act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and or severe psychological suffering to a person.
18. Victim is a woman and child who experiences and/or suffers either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
19. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the Police, Prosecutor's Office, Court, Social Institutions, or other parties who know or hear or violence against women has occurred.
20. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
21. Companion is a person who has the expertise to accompany victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
22. Optimal service is a dynamic effort consisting of various parts that are regularly related, followed by performance offered by one party to another party by providing benefits, in order to achieve the best goal.
23. Information is a message (speech or expression) or collection of messages consisting of order sequences of symbols, or meanings that can be interpreted from messages or collections of messages and can be recorded or transmitted.
24. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and or mother;
25. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and his children, and mother and her children and among people who are their dependents.
26. Society is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.

Article 13

The regional government is obligated to provide complaint services for the protection of women and children from acts of violence.

CHAPTER XI

REPORTING

Article 27

1. P2TP2A is obliged to report in writing the implementation of protection of women and children victims of violence to the Regent.
2. Reports as referred to in paragraph (1) include:
a. administration;
b. finance;
c. services; and
d. performance.
3. Submission of reports as referred to in paragraph (2) is implemented at least once every 6 (six) months.

CHAPTER VII

INSTITUTIONAL ARRANGEMENTS

Article 16

1. In the context of providing protection services to women and children from acts of violence, the regional government establishes P2TP2A as an integrated service center for the protection of women and children from acts of violence including victims of acts of violence.
2. P2TP2A as referred to in paragraph (1), functions as an integrated service center in providing protection to women and children from acts of violence.
3. Further provisions regarding the Organization and Work Procedures of P2TP2A as referred to in paragraph (1), shall be stipulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 12

Paragraph (1)
Point a
What is meant by complaint service is a series of actions carried out by the organizer of the integrated service institution to follow up on reports of acts of violence against women and children submitted by victims, families and/or the community.

Point b
What is meant by health services is an effort that includes promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative aspects.

Point c
What is meant by legal assistance is legal services provided by legal assistants or advocates to carry out the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of violence against women and children that is gender sensitive.

Point d
What is meant by repatriation is returning women and child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point or from the receiving area to the area of origin.

Point e
What is meant by social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly.

What is meant by social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.

Point f
What is meant by assistance service is that victims have the right to be accompanied by social workers at the investigation, prosecution or examination level.

Paragraph (2)
What is meant by minimum service standards is a performance benchmark for integrated service units in providing complaint handling services, health services, social rehabilitation, law enforcement and legal assistance, as well as repatriation and social reintegration for women and child victims of violence.

Paragraph (3)
Sufficiently clear.

Article 21

1. The regional government establishes partnerships with the business sector in the protection of women and children from acts of violence.
2. Partnership as referred to in paragraph (1) is conducted through:
a. notification of employment opportunity information for women victims of acts of violence;
b. education and training for women victims of acts of violence;
c. educational assistance for women and children victims of acts of violence who have been withdrawn from their education; and
d. fostering and increasing the economic independence of women victims of acts of violence.
3. Partnership as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2), shall be set forth in the form of an agreement.

CHAPTER IX

GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION

Article 22

1. The Regional Government is obliged to conduct guidance and supervision of the implementation of protection of women and children from acts of violence.
2. Guidance as referred to in paragraph (1), includes:
a. guidelines and fulfillment standards;
b. technical guidance and training;
c. provision of facilities;
d. monitoring; and
e. evaluation.
3. Guidance as referred to in paragraph (2), is in order to realize the objectives of protection of women and children from acts of violence in accordance with minimum service standards implemented by SKPD and the community.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is the Regency of Regent Barito Kuala.
2. Regional Government is the Regent together with regional apparatus as elements of the Regional Government administration of Barito Kuala Regency.
3. Family Planning, Women's Empowerment and Child Protection Agency, abbreviated as BKBP3A is the Regional Work Unit of Barito Kuala Regency.
4. Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Children, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is an integrated service unit established by the Regional Government to provide services to women and children victims of violence comprehensively through information services, assistance and legal aid, counseling services, medical services and safe houses through referrals.
5. Task Force for the Prevention and Handling of Human Trafficking Crimes, hereinafter referred to as the Task Force is a coordinating institution tasked with coordinating prevention and handling efforts of human trafficking crimes in Barito Kuala Regency.
6. Woman is a person who has female genitalia who can menstruate and become pregnant or has obtained legal status as a woman.
7. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including those in the womb.
8. Discrimination is any distinction, harassment or exclusion that is direct or indirect based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, class, social status, socio-economic status, gender, language, political beliefs that result in reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural and other aspects of life.
9. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, psychological to the victim;
10. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions. Coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life;
11. Violence against children is any act that results in misery or suffering to children physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom.
12. Domestic violence is any act against a person, especially women, that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically and or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion or deprivation of freedom unlawfully within the scope of the household;
13. Human trafficking is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud, and abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited;
14. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and or causing death.
15. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and or certain purposes.
16. Economic violence is any act that deliberately neglects family members in the form of not providing a decent living, care or maintenance.
17. Psychological violence is any act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and or severe psychological suffering to a person.
18. Victim is a woman and child who experiences and/or suffers either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
19. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the Police, Prosecutor's Office, Court, Social Institutions, or other parties who know or hear or violence against women has occurred.
20. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
21. Companion is a person who has the expertise to accompany victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
22. Optimal service is a dynamic effort consisting of various parts that are regularly related, followed by performance offered by one party to another party by providing benefits, in order to achieve the best goal.
23. Information is a message (speech or expression) or collection of messages consisting of order sequences of symbols, or meanings that can be interpreted from messages or collections of messages and can be recorded or transmitted.
24. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and or mother;
25. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and his children, and mother and her children and among people who are their dependents.
26. Society is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.

Article 12

Paragraph (1)
Point a
What is meant by complaint service is a series of actions carried out by the organizer of the integrated service institution to follow up on reports of acts of violence against women and children submitted by victims, families and/or the community.

Point b
What is meant by health services is an effort that includes promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative aspects.

Point c
What is meant by legal assistance is legal services provided by legal assistants or advocates to carry out the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of violence against women and children that is gender sensitive.

Point d
What is meant by repatriation is returning women and child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point or from the receiving area to the area of origin.

Point e
What is meant by social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly.

What is meant by social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.

Point f
What is meant by assistance service is that victims have the right to be accompanied by social workers at the investigation, prosecution or examination level.

Paragraph (2)
What is meant by minimum service standards is a performance benchmark for integrated service units in providing complaint handling services, health services, social rehabilitation, law enforcement and legal assistance, as well as repatriation and social reintegration for women and child victims of violence.

Sufficiently clear.

1. The obligations and responsibilities of the community as referred to in Article 6 letter b, shall be implemented in the form of community participation.

b. providing information and/or reporting acts of violence against women and children to law enforcement or authorized parties; and
